component.name: PageContainer
component.description: Constrained inner wrapper that centers content and applies a horizontal max-width preset mapped to Tailwind's container scale. Used inside full-bleed surfaces (Header, page bodies) to prevent content from sprawling on wide viewports while keeping the surrounding background full-width.

useCases: Wrapping the inner content of a full-bleed Header so the background spans the viewport but the heading row, subsection, and tabs constrain to a readable width
Constraining the body of a page so columns of cards, tables, or forms don't sprawl to 1920px
Standardizing horizontal padding (px-6) across pages so every screen has consistent edge spacing

commonPatterns.name: default-page-body
commonPatterns.description: Default lg width (1280px) for most app screens

commonPatterns.name: narrow-form
commonPatterns.description: sm width (768px) for settings, single-column forms, articles

commonPatterns.name: full-bleed
commonPatterns.description: No constraint — for canvas pages, builders, full-screen tables

antiPatterns.scenario: Nesting PageContainer inside another PageContainer or PageLayout
antiPatterns.reason: The outer container already constrains width; nesting creates unintended double-padding and a smaller inner width than either size suggests.
antiPatterns.alternative: Compose with PageLayout at the top level and use Stack for vertical rhythm inside.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using PageContainer inside a SidePanel.content slot
antiPatterns.reason: SidePanel is already a fixed-width constrained surface. Adding a max-width container inside compounds the constraint.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Stack for vertical rhythm inside SidePanel content. See governance LC-001.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using a raw div with max-w-7xl mx-auto px-6 in a page
antiPatterns.reason: Reinvents the primitive and bypasses the standard size scale, creating layout drift across pages.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use <PageContainer size="lg"> — same output, consistent across the system.

responsive.mobile: Always full-width with px-6 horizontal padding (max-width only kicks in above the size threshold).
responsive.desktop: Centers content via mx-auto when viewport exceeds the size's max-width.

accessibility.role: Generic container — no special ARIA roles needed
accessibility.screenReader: Transparent to screen readers — passes through children

rules: Default size is lg (max-w-7xl, 1280px) — fits most app screens
Use sm (max-w-3xl, 768px) for narrow content like forms, settings, articles
Use md (max-w-5xl, 1024px) for content-heavy single-column pages
Use xl (max-w-8xl, 1440px) for wide dashboards with high data density
Use full when content needs the entire viewport (canvas, builders, full-screen tables)
Do not nest PageContainer inside another PageContainer or PageLayout — the outer container is authoritative
Header reads its inner row constraint from the surrounding PageLayout's size; explicit contentSize on Header overrides

aiHints.context: PageContainer is the constrained inner wrapper for content inside full-bleed surfaces. Its sizes map directly onto Tailwind's container scale (3xl/5xl/7xl/8xl) so they're predictable and consistent. Default lg (1280px) covers most app screens. Use full only when you genuinely need viewport-wide content (data tables, canvas-style builders). Prefer composing PageLayout (which uses PageContainer internally) over reaching for PageContainer directly at the page level — PageLayout encodes structural intent, PageContainer just constrains width.
